title: Necklace and pouch against distress and hostile magic

dating.label: Neo-Assyrian to Seleucid witnesses
dating.note: The linked source witnesses carry Neo-Assyrian, Late Babylonian and Seleucid period labels. These date surviving manuscripts, not the composition or the ritual practice.

purpose: Prepare and place a stone-and-plant amulet for a person described as distressed and subject to hostile magic.
attribution: Practitioner unspecified in the edited master text

phases.name: Assemble the amulet
phases.idea: Stones, named ingredients, wool and a skin covering are assembled.

phases.name: Place on the patient
phases.idea: The prepared amulet is placed around the affected person’s neck.

steps.title: String the stones on flax
steps.shortDescription: String the stones named earlier in the prescription on flax thread or cord.
steps.summary: String the stones named earlier in the prescription on flax thread or cord.
steps.evidence: The source lists twelve stones but the exact identification of several named stone types is uncertain.

steps.evidence: The source calls these nine šammū, but the ingredients include items whose material identification is debated; the pilot indexes only selected named entries.
